text.p: Sparebankgruppen, a group of Norwegian savings banks, said on Monday it was bidding to take over Fokus Bank, the country's third largest commercial bank.
The group said it was bidding 73 crowns ($10.48) per share for Fokus.
It said in a statement to the Oslo Bourse the bid valued Fokus at 4.80 billion crowns.
Sparebankgruppen said it now controlled, directly or indirectly, 10 percent of Fokus.
Sparebankgruppen is owned by Sparebanken Nord-Norge, Sparebanken Midt-Norge, Sparebanken Vest, Sparebanken Rogaland and 12 other, unlisted savings banks.
It said its bid was conditional of the group acquiring more than 90 percent of Fokus and that regulatory authorities approve of the acquisition.
It said a takeover was also conditional of Fokus not acquiring mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank) .
Fokus and Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's biggest bank, are currently battling each other for BNbank, which last week decided to look into DnB's bid while postponing possible merger talks with Fokus.
Sparebankgruppen said it planned to integrate the business of Fokus, a regional bank, with the respective regional savings banks.
Fokus, which is the fruit of a series of fusions between several banks in the 1980s, would thus cease to exist.
The statement said a takeover of Fokus, which is 80 percent owned by foreign investors, would pose a significant regional consolidation in Norway's financial community.
